title: Anogenital Skin and Mucous Membrane Lesions

questions.lead_in: What is the most likely sexually transmitted disease to be the cause of the findings in the photograph?
questions.explanation: Syphilis The image shows significant keratitis and hypopyon as seen with anterior uveitis. Syphilis can have a variety of ocular manifestations including anterior uveitis, which is most commonly seen during secondary syphilis, posterior uveitis and retinitis, and interstitial keratitis that is a late sequela of congenital infection. Herpes simplex virus could also be considered in the differential diagnosis. (Image from Assessments. In Cohen J, Powderly W , Opal S, eds. Infectious Diseases. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2017.)

questions.question: Genital ulcer disease.

parts.text: Give the differential diagnosis for genital ulcer disease.

questions.model_answer: a) Infectious causes of genital ulcer disease: (1) Herpes simplex virus (HSV-1/HSV-2) — worldwide the most common cause; multiple small grouped painful vesicles/irregular ulcers, tender bilateral inguinal nodes, primary lesions resolve in ~3 weeks, recurrences in 5–12 days, minimal scarring. (2) Treponema pallidum (primary syphilis) — single indurated, clean-based, painless chancre with firm borders, painless bilateral inguinal adenopathy, heals spontaneously in 3–12 weeks; secondary disease gives condylomata lata. (3) Haemophilus ducreyi (chancroid) — tender “soft chancre” with ragged undermined edges and necrotic purulent base, little induration, unilateral or bilateral tender fluctuant buboes that may rupture; slowly destructive with scarring. (4) Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1–L3 (LGV) — transient, often unnoticed papule or HSV-like ulcer, then tender inguinal buboes; proctitis/proctocolitis with deep pelvic nodes after anal exposure. (5) Klebsiella granulomatis (granuloma inguinale/donovanosis) — firm nodules ulcerating into hypertrophic, friable, easily bleeding granulation tissue with extensive local destruction, vulvar/prepucial swelling, lymphadenopathy unusual. Consider also non-venereal causes: candidal vulvitis/balanitis, fixed drug eruption, and HPV-associated neoplasia (Bowen disease, erythroplasia of Queyrat), and note that >1 pathogen or no pathogen identified is common.

cohort_answer.text: HSV 1+2; Chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi); Syphilis; LGV; Granuloma inguinale (Klebsiella granulomatis). Table with details: HSV - multiple small grouped ulcers, incubation 2-7d, usually painful, reactive painful nodes; Chancroid - incubation 3-10d, ++ pain, unilateral painful inguinal LN can rupture/purulent; Syphilis - indurated smooth firm-bordered single ulcer, clean base, heals spontaneously, incubation 7-90d, usually painless, firm rubbery nontender nodes; LGV - Chlamydia trachomatis L1-L3, usually no visible ulcer, incubation 5-21d, usually painless, M>F clusters, painful groove sign, sinus tracts common; Granuloma inguinale - extensive progressive granulation tissue with rolled edges, incubation 7-90d, usually painless, pseudobuboes

questions.question: List 3 pathogens (genus and species) in which doxycycline can be considered for treatment for genital ulcers.
questions.question_raw: List 3 pathogens (genus and species) in which Doxycycline CAN be considered for treatment for genital ulcers.

parts.text: List 3 pathogens (genus and species) in which doxycycline can be considered for treatment for genital ulcers.

parts_raw.text: List 3 pathogens (genus and species) in which Doxycycline CAN be considered for treatment for genital ulcers.

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Treponema pallidum — doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x14 days, alternative to benzathine penicillin G for primary/secondary syphilis. (2) Chlamydia trachomatis L1–L3 (LGV) — tetracycline congener 14–21 days. (3) Klebsiella granulomatis (donovanosis) — doxycycline for 3 weeks or until lesions healed.

questions.question: Doxycycline in the treatment of genital ulcer disease.

parts.text: List 3 pathogens (genus and species) in which doxycycline can be considered for treatment for genital ulcers.

parts_raw.text: List 3 pathogens (genus and species) in which Doxycycline CAN be considered for treatment for genital ulcers.

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Treponema pallidum — doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x14 days is the standard alternative to benzathine penicillin G for primary/secondary syphilis. (2) Chlamydia trachomatis (serovars L1–L3, lymphogranuloma venereum) — tetracycline congeners are standard therapy, 14–21 days. (3) Klebsiella granulomatis (donovanosis/granuloma inguinale) — doxycycline is one of the effective agents, given for 3 weeks or until lesions heal.
